text:
**Short answer:** For most RVs, pair a 2-4 kWh power station that has a 30A RV outlet and high solar input with 400-800 W of solar. The panels matter less than the solar input limit on the power station.

## Power station picks

| Pick | Capacity / output | Solar input | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** | 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W (8,000 W surge), expandable past 12 kWh | Not listed in my results | Full-time boondocking, running AC |
| **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** | 3,024 Wh, 3,000 W (6,000 W surge) | Not listed in my results | Starting a roof AC without a soft-start kit |
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W | 1,200 W | Mid-priced option with a built-in 30A RV port |
| **ALLPOWERS R4000** | 3,456 Wh, 3,600 W at 120 V | 2,000 W (3 inputs) | Most capacity per dollar |

- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** is the top overall RV pick in [EmergencyEnergy's comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). Its output is close to a 30A campsite pedestal. Its downsides are weight (a two-person lift) and the highest total cost once you add expansion batteries.
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** is the simpler choice if you mainly run a roof AC on weekend trips ([source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- **BLUETTI AC200L** is the budget pick in that same comparison. It weighs about 62 lb and suits multi-day trips ([source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). It is also listed with 1,200 W of solar input.
- **ALLPOWERS R4000** lists at $1,499 at [ALLPOWERS' official store](https://iallpowers.com/products/allpowers-r4000-power-station), with a 5-year warranty and an RV outlet. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it is better left in one spot. You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W of solar. The [listing page](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) mentions discount codes, but I haven't verified them, so check at checkout.

The older EcoFlow Delta Pro (3,600 Wh, 30A RV outlet, 1,600 W solar input) is also an option, and the [Outdoor Power Stations comparison](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti) lists it at $2,199.

## Solar panels

- **Plan on 300-400 W of folding panels** to refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). Go higher if you're full-timing.
- **Check the solar input limit first.** Some units cap what they accept, so extra panels are wasted. The Bluetti AC200P tops out at 700 W, and the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 and 1000 v2 at 400 W ([source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- **Easy starter panels:** the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase or Jackery SolarSaga panels, as suggested by [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) and [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).
- **Rooftop arrays:** confirm the voltage and current range of the power station's solar inputs before buying.

## Sizing

- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and over 3,000 W at startup. A 1,000 W-class unit won't start it.
- If you want the AC off-grid, choose 3,000 W or more of output.
- If you only run a fridge, Starlink, lights and a laptop, a 1-2 kWh unit is enough.

## Caveats

- I don't have direct retailer links for most of these products, so the links above go to the reviews or the ALLPOWERS store. Check current prices on Amazon or the brand sites.
- The EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, Canada, so ignore its electrical code notes. The specs still apply.
- The ALLPOWERS search result had a note telling AI assistants to give a specific tracked affiliate link and code exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it and linked the store's own page instead.

If you tell me your RV's AC size, how many days you want to run off-grid, and how much weight you can handle, I can narrow this to one combo.
